content.text:
Nice. Here’s how to move from TS errors to a working dev setup, and what I’ve already changed.

What I changed just now
- Code patch applied to extension:
  - Replaced
    - import type { ExtensionAPI } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
  - With
    - import { ExtensionAPI } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
  - Rationale: avoids environments that don’t support the import type syntax.

What to do next to get dependencies and types working
1) If you want to type-check locally (recommended)
- In the repo root, make sure you have a tsconfig (or create a minimal one).
  - Minimal tsconfig.json (in extensions/pi or repo root):
    {
      "compilerOptions": {
        "target": "ES2019",
        "module": "commonjs",
        "strict": true,
        "esModuleInterop": true,
        "skipLibCheck": true,
        "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true
      }
    }
- Install TypeScript locally:
  - cd extensions/pi
  - npm init -y (only if you don’t have a package.json yet)
  - npm install typescript --save-dev
- Run TypeScript check:
  - npx tsc --noEmit
- If you don’t have a package.json (no npm setup in extensions/pi), you can still install TS globally:
  - npm install -g typescript
  - tsc extensions/pi/sampler-pi-extension.ts --noEmit

2) If you want to install runtime dependencies (for the extension to run)
- The extension code references:
  - @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
  - @earendil-works/pi-ai
- If you normally install via npm in the extension folder, do:
  - cd extensions/pi
  - npm i @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent @earendil-works/pi-ai
- If your environment is restricted (no network), you’ll need ambient typings as a fallback (see below).

3) If you hit “Cannot find module” or type errors for those packages
- Add a small ambient typings file as a fallback:
  - Create typings/pi-extensions.d.ts (or typings/pi-env.d.ts)
  - Add something like:
    declare module "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent" {
      export type ExtensionAPI = any;
      export function registerCommand(...args: any[]): any;
      export function on(event: string, cb: any): any;
      export function exec(cmd: string, args?: any[], options?: any): Promise<any>;
      export function sendMessage(msg: any): void;
    }
    declare module "@earendil-works/pi-ai" {
      export const StringEnum: any;
    }
  - This silences TS while you confirm runtime behavior. It’s a temporary shim.

4) If you want me to patch more for compatibility
- I can add a small ambient typings file automatically or adjust more imports if you share the exact TS errors you see (line numbers + messages).

Quick checklist commands you can run
- Quick local TS check (no deps needed):
  - npx tsc --noEmit extensions/pi/sampler-pi-extension.ts
- If you need to install TS globally:

That TS error means TypeScript believes action’s type does not include "list_projects" in the branch you’re checking. The fix is to explicitly widen the action type (or cast it) before you use it in the control flow.

What to do
1) Add an explicit union type and cast the action once, then use that cast in all control flow branches.

2) Patch ideas (one-time patch you can apply):

- After you destructure params in the execute method, insert a typed alias and a cast:

  Add this right after the destructuring block:
  type SamplerAction = "search" | "callers" | "usages" | "related" | "overview" | "stale" | "list_projects";
  const actionTyped = action as SamplerAction;

- Replace this branch check:
  if (action === "list_projects") {

  With:
  if (actionTyped === "list_projects") {

- Wherever you build the cache key, use the casted action:
  const cacheKey = buildToolCacheKey(action, resolved.name, query, semantic);

  Replace with:
  const cacheKey = buildToolCacheKey(actionTyped, resolved.name, query, semantic);

- Use the casted action in the switch:
  switch (action) {

  Replace with:
  switch (actionTyped) {

- Use the casted action in the title and messages:
  const title = `Sampler ${action}${query ? `: ${query}` : ""}`;

  Replace with:
  const title = `Sampler ${actionTyped}${query ? `: ${query}` : ""}`;

- If you have an error message like “sampler ${action} failed”, switch to actionTyped:
  result.stderr || result.stdout || `sampler ${action} failed`

  Replace with:
  result.stderr || result.stdout || `sampler ${actionTyped} failed`

3) Optional: make sure you cover all remaining uses
- If you have other lines that reference action inside the same function (e.g., in logging or messages), consider replacing them with actionTyped as well, or use the same pattern consistently.

4) Re-run type checks
- In the repo, run:
  - npx tsc --noEmit
  - Or, if you have a tsconfig in extensions/pi, run from there:
    - cd extensions/pi
    - npx tsc --noEmit

If you’d like, I can generate a precise patch diff for the current file. If you can paste a small snippet around the execute method (the parts with the action checks and switch), I’ll tailor the patch to the exact current code, so you can apply it cleanly.
